To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

, for a rotatable central composite design with an observation missing, the variance of a response predicted at any design point is inflated by a factor that is a function of the angle formed by two vectors of factor levels at which the response is predicted and an observation is missing.
, for rotatble central composite design, the inflation amount depends only on the two vectors and the angle formed between the two vectors.

the prediction variance of a central compostie design is inflated when an obervation is missing and that the amount of the inflation is proportional to the squared length of the missing vector and inversely proportional to the cosine of the angle formed by that vector and the vector at which the response is predicted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction variance in central composite designs and provides an expression for it.
the prediction variance of a response surface design with a missing observation.

how much the variance is inflated when an experiment is conducted under an experimental design with missing observation and how the inflation amount of a predicted response depends on the experimental design and the missing observation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prediction variance of a rotatable central composite design is not much inflated by the loss of one observation, as long as the observation is missing at a point far from the design center.
the inflation amount of a prediction variance is a function of the Euclidean norms of two vectors of factor levels and the angle formed between the two vectors.

, if a rotatable central composite design is used and the observation is missing at the center of the design, the prediction variance is inflated by a factor of 1/3, if the observation is missing in one of the four vertices of a cube, the prediction variance will be inflated by a factor ranging from 1/4 to 1/2, if the observation at the center of a cube is missing, the prediction variance would be inflated by a much higher factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inflation amount of a prediction variance is a function of the Euclidean norms of the two vectors and the cosine of the angle formed by them, and the inflation amount is larger when the angle is smaller.

, for rotatability, the prediction variance is inflated when a missing observation is located in the middle region of a design and is deflated when a missing observation occurs at the corner region of a design.
the prediction variance of rotatable central composite design with one missing observation is inflated by the same amount as that of a full factorial design with the same number of observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for rotatability, the inflation amount depends only on the two vectors, and it is a function of their inner product and the Euclidean norms.

the inflation amount of prediction variance is not affected by the number of missing observations, the number of design points, the number of runs, the number of factors, and the number of levels of each factor.
the prediction variance is more likely to be inflated if the two vectors of the factor values are more orthogonal to each other.
